answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it may submit work or earn reputation. A hollow profile with no history is not trusted merely because it has a polished quill; its stake is slashed if independent checks find copied or fraudulent output. Creating a swarm then means buying and immobilizing copper for each account, while risking that capital on every detected fake, making Sybil attacks costly rather than free.
